package_info.package_versions: 2019.4 HF 5 and others released between March and June 2020
package_info.why_malicious: The Orion software update was compromised by attackers who inserted malicious code (known as Sunburst) into the update package. This code enabled remote access to customer environments, exfiltration of sensitive data, and lateral movement, affecting thousands of organizations including government agencies. The malicious code was not part of the legitimate Orion product and was designed to evade detection and enable espionage.

execution_context.trigger: At import-time (service startup) and periodically at runtime (scheduled beaconing intervals)
execution_context.file_location: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll (compiled into the update package, typically located in the Orion installation directory)
required_permissions: environment_vars (read system and user environment variables)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time and on a periodic schedule during runtime, the code collects environment and system information, encodes it, and sends it via HTTP to the hardcoded C2 domain avsvmcloud.com, then awaits and executes remote commands received from the attacker, enabling persistent remote access and control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code initiates unsolicited outbound HTTP connections to a hardcoded external domain (avsvmcloud.com), exfiltrates encoded environment and system data, and implements a remote command execution backdoor within a critical Orion service process.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Orion updates should not contain code that establishes covert C2 channels, exfiltrates internal environment details, or allows arbitrary remote command execution by unauthorized parties. Such behavior is inconsistent with standard update or telemetry functionality.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate software may contact vendor servers for update checks or telemetry, but should not transmit detailed environment/system data or accept and execute arbitrary commands from external sources.
key_indicators: Presence of hardcoded C2 domain (avsvmcloud.com) in Orion DLL
Encoded or encrypted environment/system information sent in outbound HTTP requests
Orion process (BusinessLayerHost) performing periodic, stealthy beaconing to external infrastructure
Capability to receive and execute arbitrary commands from C2 server
Delayed activation and obfuscated network traffic to evade detection

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is inserted into the Orion update package and distributed to customers via the standard SolarWinds update mechanism.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code on customer systems upon installation or update

attack_chain.action: Upon installation or service startup, the malicious SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll loads and initiates periodic beaconing to the attacker's command-and-control server (avsvmcloud.com), sending encoded environment and system information.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishment of covert C2 channel and profiling of victim environment

attack_chain.action: The attacker issues commands via the C2 channel, which are received and executed by the compromised Orion process, enabling remote code execution, lateral movement, and data exfiltration within the victim's network.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of the environment and facilitation of espionage operations

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound HTTP/S requests to avsvmcloud.com or related C2 domains from SolarWinds Orion processes (e.g., BusinessLayerHost.exe)
Encoded or encrypted environment/system data present in HTTP request payloads originating from Orion servers
Orion process spawning unexpected child processes or executing commands not typical for normal operation
Delayed or periodic network beaconing behavior from Orion services
file_indicators: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll with anomalous code sections or function exports not present in legitimate versions
Presence of DLLs in the Orion installation directory with unexpected digital signatures or hash mismatches compared to official SolarWinds releases
Timestamp anomalies or unexpected file modification dates on Orion DLLs
network_indicators: Outbound connections to avsvmcloud.com and associated C2 infrastructure domains/IPs from Orion servers
Unusual HTTP/S traffic patterns from Orion servers to external IPs/domains, especially with encoded payloads
DNS queries for avsvmcloud.com or related C2 domains from Orion server hosts
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Orion server processes for unexpected outbound network connections, especially to known C2 domains such as avsvmcloud.com. Inspect SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll and related DLLs for unauthorized code changes, hash mismatches, or anomalous exports. Analyze network traffic from Orion services for encoded or suspicious payloads and periodic beaconing patterns. Alert on Orion processes executing commands or spawning child processes outside of normal operational profiles. Correlate file, process, and network indicators to identify compromised Orion installations.
